hero.lede: Hold a key, ask about whatever is on screen, and the answer arrives in place. No tab switching, no copying context.
hero.title: Revenue by region
marquee.label: What Spirit does
product.title: The answer should arrive where you are looking.
product.body: Most tools ask you to leave the thing you are working on, find a chat box, describe the screen, then carry the answer back. Spirit removes the trip.

product.scene.body: The close pack is below. One row is pulling its total from the wrong column.

cards.0.title: Read the screen, not the window.
cards.0.body: A screenshot, the text layer and the accessibility tree are compared before the model answers. It knows which table cell you meant, even when two rows look identical.
cards.1.title: Answer where you are looking.
cards.1.body: The reply opens beside the cursor with the actions that follow from it. Copy it, save it, or point at the exact row it came from. Nothing moves to a sidebar.
cards.2.title: Act on the next click.
cards.2.body: Spirit can click, type, scroll and press keys through the same input driver the app exposes, so the follow-up happens instead of being described back to you.
how.title: It reads, answers, acts.
how.body: The whole product is one gesture. These are the three parts that make it feel like the computer is listening.
inside.title: What’s inside.
inside.body: The parts you would otherwise assemble yourself, already working together.
inside.0.title: Screen reading
inside.0.body: Screenshot, OCR and the accessibility tree are combined into one scene. The model sees the table cell, the button label and the window around them.
inside.1.title: Models
inside.1.body: Bring an OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter or local key. Spirit routes each request and keeps the keys in the encrypted store.
inside.2.title: Voice
inside.2.body: Hold to talk. Whisper transcribes locally while you speak, and the answer can be read back in place without leaving the app.
inside.3.title: Actions
inside.3.body: Click, type, scroll, drag and press keys through the input driver. The model calls the same functions the app exposes, with a native fallback.
inside.4.title: Memory
inside.4.body: Session context and long-term notes are recalled with BM25, synonyms and fuzzy matching. Everything stays on disk, under your control.
asked.title: Things people ask.
asked.body: The questions are ordinary. The difference is that Spirit can see what you are pointing at.
wall.label: Questions people ask Spirit
wall.0.0: What does this error mean, and which line is actually wrong?
wall.0.1: Summarize this page without the cookie banner and the footer.
wall.0.2: Which of these two plans is cheaper after the annual discount?
wall.0.3: Translate this paragraph and keep the technical terms.
wall.1.0: Why did revenue dip in March if the quarter is up?
wall.1.1: Find the cell that feeds this chart and change it to 12%.
wall.1.2: What is this button called in the app I am looking at?
wall.1.3: Rewrite this paragraph in plain English, same length.
wall.2.0: Point at the setting that turns off automatic updates.
wall.2.1: Compare this diff and tell me what could break.
wall.2.2: What is the keyboard shortcut for the thing I just clicked?
wall.2.3: Is this email asking me to pay, or just confirming the order?
process.title: Point. Ask. Read.
steps.0.title: Hold
steps.0.body: Press Alt + Space anywhere. Spirit reads what is under the cursor, not the whole screen.
steps.1.title: Ask
steps.1.body: Type or speak. The question stays attached to the thing you pointed at.
steps.2.title: Read
steps.2.body: The answer lands beside the cursor. Press escape and it is gone.
cta.body: One binary, a native capsule and your own model key. Install it, point at something, and ask.
faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.body: The things people check before they install. Everything else is in the manual.
faq.0.title: Does Spirit send my screen anywhere?
faq.0.body: Only to the model you configure. Screenshots and OCR text go with the request; nothing is stored on our side. With a local model, the whole loop stays on the machine.
faq.1.title: Which models can I use?
faq.1.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter and local runtimes behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Keys stay in the encrypted store.
faq.2.title: Does it work offline?
faq.2.body: Screen reading, OCR and voice transcription run locally. Answers need a model; a local model keeps the whole loop offline.
faq.3.title: What are the system requirements?
faq.3.body: Windows 10 or 11, macOS 13 or newer, or a modern Linux desktop. Four gigabytes of RAM for the app, more for a local model.
faq.4.title: How do I change the hotkey?
faq.4.body: Settings, then Shortcuts. Hold, toggle and voice keys are separate, and conflicts are reported before a change is saved.
faq.5.title: Is it free?
faq.5.body: The app is free for personal, educational, and internal business use under the Business Source License 1.1. You may read and modify the source. Hosting it as a service, white-labeling it, or redistributing it commercially requires a separate written license. The license converts to Apache 2.0 on 2030-11-01.
docs.title: Manual.
docs.lede: Everything Spirit does, in one page. Install it, learn the gesture, and know exactly what leaves your machine.
docs.toc.label: On this page
docs.install.title: Install
docs.install.body1: Grab the build for your platform, or run it from source. Spirit needs a screen capture permission on macOS the first time it reads the cursor area.
docs.install.body2: The packaged app installs to {mac} on macOS and {win} on Windows.
docs.use.title: Use it
docs.use.body1: Hold the hotkey. The capsule appears next to the cursor and starts listening. Type or speak your question, then release.
docs.use.body2: Spirit captures the region around the pointer, reads text and UI elements, and sends only what is needed to the model you configured.
docs.demo.title: Demo mode
docs.demo.body1: Demo mode keeps the model from touching your real screen. The answer is generated from the captured context only, and it is labelled as a demo in the capsule.
docs.demo.body2: Use it when you are presenting, recording, or testing a provider without sending anything to the live machine.
docs.ghost.title: Ghost mode
docs.ghost.body1: Ghost mode hides Spirit from screen capture and screen sharing, and removes the tray icon. It is on by default; toggle it in Settings or press Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G on macOS).
docs.ghost.body2: On Windows and macOS the overlay windows are excluded at the OS level, so they do not appear in screenshots, recordings, or shared screens. Linux has no equivalent capture-exclusion API, so only the tray and taskbar hiding apply there.
docs.ghost.body3: Spirit stays visible in Task Manager, and any other app that enumerates windows can still detect it. Ghost mode is privacy for your audience, not a security boundary.

faq.page.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.6.title: Can Spirit click the wrong thing?
faq.6.body: It can. The model draws its targets from a screenshot and the accessibility tree, and either can mis-read a busy screen. That is why every click, keypress and paste shows an approval card first — read it, then allow. Denying is always one press and nothing breaks.
faq.7.title: Does it read my passwords?
faq.7.body: Spirit only reads what is under your cursor when you trigger it. If you hold the hotkey while a password field is in the capture, that text goes to your model provider like any other context — so don't ask questions with credentials on screen. Spirit's own keys stay encrypted in your OS keychain.
faq.8.title: What does a question cost?
faq.8.body: Whatever your provider charges for the tokens — typically a fraction of a cent on small models. The OpenRouter models Spirit ships with are free. Use a local model and it costs nothing but electricity.
faq.9.title: Windows shows a SmartScreen warning when I install
faq.9.body: That is because the installer is not code-signed yet — SmartScreen flags any unsigned download. Click More info, then Run anyway, or grab the build from the official GitHub releases. Signing is wired up and switches on as soon as a certificate is configured.
faq.10.title: Does it work over games?
faq.10.body: In windowed or borderless mode, usually yes. Exclusive fullscreen games can block overlays entirely, and some anti-cheat systems dislike input automation — use it for browsing, documents and dev tools, not ranked matches.
faq.11.title: How do I wipe everything Spirit knows?
faq.11.body: Open the Memory panel to delete single takeaways, or delete the workspace folder and config.json in app data to erase sessions, memory and settings completely. Uninstalling never silently wipes your files.
faq.12.title: Can I use my company's OpenAI key?
faq.12.body: Yes — the key stays in your machine's keychain and requests go straight from your machine to the provider. Do check your company policy on what may be sent to that provider, since your prompts and screen context travel with the question.
faq.13.title: Why is the answer sometimes wrong?
faq.13.body: Because models are statistical, not factual databases. Screen context keeps answers grounded in what is actually on your display, but for anything that matters — numbers, names, commands that delete things — treat the answer as a draft and verify.
faq.14.title: Does Spirit show up in screen recordings?
faq.14.body: Not on Windows or macOS while Ghost mode is on — the overlay windows are excluded from capture, and the tray icon is hidden. Linux has no capture-exclusion API, so Spirit can still appear there. Ghost mode does not hide the process from Task Manager.
doc.g-start.title: Getting started
doc.g-start.plain: Install Spirit, add a model key, and ask your first question. Two minutes, no account.
doc.g-trigger.title: The trigger — hold, ask, release
doc.g-trigger.plain: One gesture controls Spirit: hold the hotkey and the capsule opens at your cursor. Type or speak, let go, and the answer streams in right where you were looking.
doc.g-ask.title: Asking well — chips, commands, regions
doc.g-ask.plain: You do not have to type everything. Spirit suggests questions based on your screen, understands slash commands, and lets you paint a region to ask about.
doc.g-voice.title: Talking to Spirit
doc.g-voice.plain: Hold the mic and speak — Spirit writes your words into the prompt. With the local speech model installed, your voice never leaves the computer. It answers out loud, highlighting each word as it is spoken.
doc.g-memory.title: What Spirit remembers
doc.g-memory.plain: Every answer leaves behind short takeaways. Next time you ask something related, the relevant ones come back — so you never repeat yourself. You can see, edit and delete every memory.
doc.g-act.title: Letting Spirit act — approvals without fear
doc.g-act.plain: Spirit can click, type, open apps and run commands for you. Anything that changes something asks first with a plain approval card. You always see exactly what will happen before it does.
doc.g-privacy-plain.title: Your data in plain words
doc.g-privacy-plain.plain: No telemetry, no analytics, no cloud storage, no account. Your conversations and memories are files on your machine. The only time data leaves is when you ask a question — then it goes to the AI provider you chose.
doc.g-troubleshoot.title: When something is off
doc.g-troubleshoot.plain: Most rough edges have a one-line fix. Start here before digging deeper.
doc.overview.title: Overview — what Spirit is
doc.overview.plain: Spirit is a desktop app that lives next to your cursor. Hold a key, ask a question, and it answers with awareness of whatever is on your screen at that spot. It can also act for you — click, type, open apps — but only when you approve.
doc.trigger-flow.title: Trigger-to-answer flow
doc.trigger-flow.plain: This is the journey of a single question: from the moment you press the hotkey to the moment the answer finishes typing itself in front of you.
doc.capture.title: Screen reading — capture, OCR, scene graph
doc.capture.plain: Spirit "sees" by taking a small screenshot around your cursor, reading the text in it with OCR, and asking the operating system what app, window and UI elements are there. None of this leaves your machine by itself.
doc.input-engine.title: Input engine — how Spirit clicks and types
doc.input-engine.plain: When you approve an action, Spirit moves the cursor, clicks, types and scrolls for you. There are two engines: a built-in one that talks to the OS directly, and a faster vendored driver. If the driver ever fails, Spirit quietly falls back without breaking your question.
doc.annotations.title: Annotations — arrows and boxes on your screen
doc.annotations.plain: Sometimes the best answer is pointing. The model can draw arrows, boxes and dots directly over your apps — here is how a sentence from an AI becomes a shape floating over your screen.
doc.providers.title: AI providers and the router
doc.providers.plain: Spirit does not include AI — you bring your own key. You can stack several providers; if the first is down or rate-limited, the next one takes over automatically. Use a local model and nothing ever leaves your machine.
doc.tools.title: Tools and the approval system
doc.tools.plain: Spirit can act, not just answer — 27 tools from "read my clipboard" to "run a shell command". Anything that changes something asks you first with an approval card. Two dangerous tools always ask, no matter what you have allowed before.
doc.memory.title: Memory — takeaways, sessions, app lessons
doc.memory.plain: Spirit remembers. Every answer leaves behind short "takeaways" it can recall later when relevant, your conversations are saved as files you can open, and it even learns the quirks of the apps you use.
doc.voice.title: Voice — speaking and listening
doc.voice.plain: Hold the mic and talk; Spirit transcribes and answers out loud in a natural voice. With the local speech model installed, your voice never leaves the computer. It can even wake when you say "Hey Spirit".
doc.renderer.title: Renderer — the pill, hooks and IPC bridge
doc.renderer.plain: Everything you see — the pill that follows your cursor, the answer box, the settings — is one small React app. It never touches the network or your files directly; every capability goes through a tightly guarded bridge.
doc.security.title: Security and privacy engineering
doc.security.plain: The promises on the Privacy page are enforced in code: your keys are encrypted with your operating system keyring, the UI sandbox cannot reach the internet, links cannot be used to probe your network, and AI-generated files pass a strict sanitizer.
doc.storage.title: Storage — what lives where
doc.storage.plain: Everything Spirit keeps is in two places you control: an app-data folder for settings and a workspace folder you picked for your sessions and memory. Delete them and Spirit simply starts fresh.
doc.packaging.title: Building and packaging
doc.packaging.plain: How Spirit goes from source code to the installers on the Download page: one command per platform, with code signing and notarization switched on by environment variables only — no secrets ever live in the repository.
doc.testing.title: Testing and quality gates
doc.testing.plain: Spirit tests the thinking parts — the parsers, scorers and planners — with fast unit tests, and any change must pass a type check plus those tests before it counts as done.
doc.debugging.title: Debug logging
doc.debugging.plain: When Spirit misbehaves in a development build, every run leaves a diary: what you asked, what the model saw, which tools ran. Packaged builds write none of this.
doc.source.title: Source map — where things live
doc.source.plain: A map of the repository for developers and the curious: which folder does what, and where to look for the interesting bits.
